inlines.text: The table shows the income tax rates for the 2020-2021 financial year.
Rachel has a gross annual salary of $91 500.
She has allowable tax deductions of $1350 for a laptop and $620 for professional memberships.
Calculate the total tax payable by Rachel. Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Taxable income} &= 91\,500-1350-620\\\text{Taxable income} &= \$89\,530\end{align*}$$
This is the third tax bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Excess} &= 89\,530-45\,000\\\text{Excess} &= \$44\,530\\\text{Tax payable} &= 5092+0.325\times44\,530\\\text{Tax payable} &= \$19\,564.25\end{align*}$$

payloads.replacement:
- **Tax** is money you pay to the government to fund government services.
- **Income tax** is tax the government collects from individuals.
- Income tax is a **percentage** of your **annual taxable income**.
- The **Australian Taxation Office (ATO)** collects taxes.

The total income you receive from all sources before tax or deductions are taken out.

This includes income from work (full-time, part-time or casual), interest or dividends from investments, and rent from property you own.

$\text{Taxable income}=\text{Gross income}-\text{Allowable tax deductions}$

Round taxable income down to the nearest whole dollar.

**Allowable tax deductions** are expenses you subtract from gross income. They include:
- Work-related expenses, when all of these apply:
  - The expense relates directly to earning your income.
  - You paid for it yourself and were not reimbursed.
  - You have a receipt or invoice to prove it.
- Donations to charity.
- Union fees.
- Tax agent fees.
- Allowable tax deductions differ depending on your job.
The new tax rate, called the **marginal tax rate**, applies only to each [[additional|32]] dollar you earn above \$120,000.
Most people pay income tax through [[pay as you go|35]] (PAYG).

- **Medicare** is Australia's universal healthcare scheme. A doctor's visit is either free or the government pays a large percentage of the cost.
- The government partly funds Medicare through an **additional tax** called the **Medicare levy**.
